Kahit Matindi ang Sikat ng Araw, Tuloy-Tuloy ang Serbisyo ng DSWD sa Masbate

Sa kabila ng matinding sikat ng araw, patuloy ang DSWD Field Office (FO) 5 - Bicol Region sa paglo-load ng mga non-food items (NFIs) na dinala nitong Linggo, Oktubre 5 sa mga lokal na pamahalaan ng Mobo, Cataingan, Palanas, Dimasalang, Milagros at Masbate City para sa mga Masbateno na sinalanta ng bagyong #OpongPH.

Ang 2,200 NFIs na na-deliver ay binubuo ng 200 Water Filtration Kits, 200 Hygiene Kits, 200 Family Kits, 200 Kitchen Kits, 200 Malong, 200 Mosquito Nets at 1,000 Jerry Cans. Kaagapay ng DSWD FO-5 ang Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) at Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) sa mabilis at maayos na operasyon hnggang sa aktwal na pamamahagi sa mga komunidad.

Patuloy ang DSWD, sa pamumuno ni Secretary @rex_gatchalian , sa paghahatid ng serbisyong maagap, mapagkalinga at may kasamang malasakit. Alinsunod ito sa atas ni Pangulong Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. para sa agarang tulong sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo hanggang sa kanilang pagbangon.

#BawatBuhayMahalagaSaDSWD❤️

TRAFFIC ADVISORY
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

06 October 2025

TRAVIS SCOTT CIRCUS MAXIMUS WORLD TOUR CONCERT AT FNB STADIUM, NASREC, JOHANNESBURG

The Johannesburg Metropolitan Police Department (JMPD) wishes to inform the public about traffic disruptions expected around the FNB Stadium Precinct due to the Travis Scott Circus Maximus World Tour Concert taking place on Saturday, 11 October, 2025.

The concert is expected to start at 8:30 PM (20:30) and end at approximately 11:00 PM (23:00)

Early arrivals will be expected from 09:00 and Gates will open at 16:00.

​All Hospitality and VIP ticket holders are strongly encouraged to arrive early to ensure smooth access and avoid potential traffic delays closer to the start of the show.

Road Closures:

The JMPD will implement full road closures starting at 11:00 AM to manage traffic flow around the FNB Stadium. Please note the following affected roads:

- Soweto Highway
- Golden Highway
- Nasrec Road
- Booysens Reserve Road

Specific Road Closure Details:
  
- Golden Highway: Closed between the Corner of Golden Highway, Ring 1, and Soweto Highway. Only authorised vehicles will be allowed access.

- Nasrec Road: Closed between Recreation Road and Shaft 17 Road. Access to pre-paid parking is available at Recreation Road.

- Soweto Highway: Closed between Mentz Street and the N1 Offramp.

- Booysens Reserve Road: Closed between Crownwood Road and League Avenue.

Transportation Options:

To enhance your travel experience, we recommend the following options:

- Park and Ride: This option is highly encouraged for stress-free travel. Secure, undercover parking and return transport are available at several points, including:

   - Sandton City
   - Melrose Arch
   - Centurion Mall
   - Montecasino
   - Clearwater Mall
   - Cresta Shopping Centre
   - Greenstone Shopping Centre
   - Mall of Africa
   - Menlyn Park
   - East Rand Mall
   - The Glen Shopping Centre
   - Gold Reef City Casino
   - The Grove Mall

- Gautrain: Trains and buses will operate with increased frequency to accommodate concert-goers from Park Station to FNB and back to Park Station.

- E-hailing & Drop & Go: A designated drop-off area for ride-sharing services will be available.

Residents are encouraged to be aware of traffic management for the day so they can plan their travel routes accordingly. We further urge residents to exercise patience before, during, and after the concert, especially after the concert when traffic congestion may be significant.

We further encourage all patrons to plan their travel in advance as well and take advantage of the designated transportation options to ensure a safe and enjoyable concert experience.

-END-

Issued by the Johannesburg Metropolitan Police Department Communication Unit #JoburgRoadSafety #JHBTraffic #SaferJoburg #NomakanjaniManjeNamhlanje #TravisScott

data.raw_text:
You may have never heard of them before, but these are the Manila Martyrs who were killed by the Japanese in WW2.

On February 3rd, 1945, U.S. troops broke through the gates of Santo Tomas and liberated the 3,677 emaciated internees, 480 of whom were children under the age of ten. They were just in time, as their food stores were nearly empty, and the supply of cats, rats, pigeons and weeds that had previously sustained them were exhausted.

With the liberation of Santo Tomas, MacArthur thought the war was over. He expected Manila to be an “open city” and anticipated a victory parade. However, the rest of the sprawling city, home to one million Filipino men, women, and children, remained under the control of Japanese troops, who were about to embark on a desperate and brutal killing spree.

They carried out systematic mass executions of men, women, children and members of religious orders by beheading, bayoneting, clubbing, hanging, burning alive, drowning and death by explosives.

They inflicted unimaginable torture, r*ped women and girls of all ages, many of whom were mutilated or killed in the process and ripped unborn babies from their mothers’ wombs. In the background was the rattle of Japanese machine guns and the thunder of American artillery.

General Iwabuchi sealed all the gates of the walled city of Manila, and set it ablaze. It became a raging inferno as one section after another caught fire.

Soon after, American artillery began shelling the Malate and nearby Ermita districts. Most of the houses were made of wood, and soon, the district was burning, block by block.

The people of Manila were caught in a vice-grip between their oppressors and their liberators; if they remained in their homes, they risked being burned alive, and if they ventured outside, they faced the threat of Japanese snipers.

On February 7th, the Japanese looted and set fire to Malate church and presbytery. Fathers Henaghan, Kelly, Fallon, and Monaghan were arrested and taken to the nearby Syquia Apartments. Reports as to how they died vary. A Maryknoll nun, who was in Manila at the time, gave a harrowing account of their deaths to Professor James T Carroll of Iona University, New York in 1995 - “the Filipino guerrillas were assisted by the Irish Columban Fathers who maintained their cover well into the war. When the Japanese discovered that they were not pro-Japanese, they nailed them to the church doors”.

Fr Lalor was working that day and escaped arrest but was killed along with 200 others on February 13th when American troops shelled the hospital.

In all, sixty priests and Brothers were murdered in a brutal and cold-blooded series of executions by the Japanese.

The “Vatican City” was liberated on February 23rd in a daring and high-risk rescue by the combined Eleventh Airborne Division of the United States Army and Filipino guerrillas. The 2,132 starving inmates were rescued just minutes before they were scheduled to be executed.

What remained of the beautiful city of Manila, once known as the Pearl of the Orient, was liberated on March 3rd.

Collectively known as the “Malate Martyrs”, the Columbans chose to remain with their people throughout the savage Japanese occupation, saving the lives of many and bringing spiritual comfort to countless others.

$GRAB Tourism & GrabMap Flywheel 🧵

TLDR: Bullish. For those that want shorter version: "B"

Grab Holdings Limited AI SuperApp, Southeast Asia's leading superapp, has transformed from a ride-hailing disruptor into a multifaceted ecosystem encompassing mobility, deliveries, financial services, and now, aggressively, tourism and mapping technologies. Operating in eight countries (Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam), Grab serves over 46 million monthly transacting users. 

Launched in 2022 as an in-house alternative to costly third-party providers like Google Maps, GrabMaps has evolved into a hyperlocal, AI-powered platform tailored to SEA's chaotic urban-rural mix: informal roads, dynamic traffic, and 65 million+ points of interest (POIs) like street vendors. By Q3 2022, it fully powered Grab's operations, saving millions in licensing fees and enabling 15-20% fuel efficiency gains for drivers (translating to higher earnings and retention).

With 150m travelers a year in SEA, and soon to grow to 250m visitors by 2030, GrabMap monetization will be massive to enhance GrabAds segment. Particaularly through  Promoted listings, Grab ads Map interface, APIs, Commission & licensing fees( @amazon , @Microsoft , @Huawei), Subscription for businesses. 

Grab Tourism isn't a standalone app but an embedded ecosystem leveraging the superapp for end-to-end travel: airport transfers, attraction bookings, bundled deals, and payments. A 2025 Grab study shows 1 in 2 SEA tourists already use the app, drawn by "one-app convenience" (15-20% higher retention). With ASEAN tourism rebounding to $375 billion in mobility/delivery spend alone (from 150 million visitors), Grab is embedding affordability via BNPL and partnerships to convert impulse travelers. Recent partnership with @Alipay with 1.7B users or @KlookTravel  will only accelerate this growth. 

Meaning, GrabMap will be able to sell much more ads due to the massive tourism market share. Meaning small to mega cap businesses will spend more to appear more hightlighted to travelers. This could add much more monthly transacting users to 100-150m a month. Noted that visitors tend to use more premium services on Grab SuperApp, and more frequently(4-5 more time than domestic). 

Ok now the juicy part, Can we hit $1B revenue by Q4?

For 2026, Forbes analysts forecast $5-6B revenue (42-71% growth), driven by 30-50% tourism expansion ($500M-1B add) and Maps scaling. EBITDA could hit $800M-1B (41% margin expansion in FinTech), with EPS turning positive at $0.04. @Forbes is even more bullish than my projection. 

Path to $1B Revenue in Q4 2025:

~Core Growth (70% of uplift): 20-25% YoY from mobility/deliveries ($5B+ GMV), ads (1.7% of Deliveries GMV, +31% active advertisers), and GrabUnlimited subscriptions.
~Tourism Contribution (15-20%): $200-250M from bundles/BNPL (10-15% of $1.1B digital payments target); 20-25% ride spikes in peaks.
~Maps B2B (5-10%): $20-50M from API/licensing (e.g., Mongolia/Tino); high margins offset incentives.
~Catalysts: Fed rate cuts (2-2.5% FFR by 2026) weaken USD, boosting SEA currencies (Grab earns in 8); short interest drop (178M shares) reduces pressure.
~Dine out explosive growth, due to solving the "want" from users(will link the thread I wrote on this below)

Conclusion: GrabMaps and Tourism are not siloed bets but symbiotic forces turbocharging Grab's superapp flywheel: Maps enables precise, safe travel; Tourism funnels high-value spend (2-3x daily rides) into the ecosystem. 

With SEA's digital/tourism boom, these could deliver the $1B Q4 milestone and 30-50% 2026 growth, re-rating Grab to a 10-15x P/S ($70-80B market cap). CEO Anthony Tan's "triple bottom line" obsession—empowering users, drivers, and merchants as customers(Secret sauce) positions Grab as SEA's indispensable platform, akin to WeChat but with deeper economic uplift. For investors, this is an inflection: from survival to dominance.

Not Financial Advice!
